thought.text: The guide's image `codeberg.org/kosmos-eu/open_taki:latest` is available. Now let me check how `/rmeta/text` expects requests, so I can do a functional verification later:

reasoning_content:
The image is available: `codeberg.org/kosmos-eu/open_taki:latest` (tags: 20260819-1601, 20260819-2138, latest). The guide says to use `codeberg.org/kosmos-eu/open_taki:latest` — this matches.

Now, the guide's flow presupposes an OpenCloud compose stack, which we don't have. The essence of the installation:
1. Get the open_taki service running (as a container) using a config file (taki-config.yaml) at /etc/open_taki/config.yaml
2. Verify: curl http://localhost:9998/ → {"name":"open_taki","version":...,"features":{...}}

Plan:
1. Write taki-config.yaml in the workspace (based on the guide, but since this environment has no LLM/Collabora services, use an unreachable but structurally valid placeholder. Or better, leave it empty/point to a local URL. The health endpoint reports the configured value. The "Minimal setup" in the guide says just llm is sufficient).
2. Pull the image codeberg.org/kosmos-eu/open_taki:latest.
3. Run the container with port 9998 exposed, mounting the config to /etc/open_taki/config.yaml:ro (as the guide specifies).
4. Verify: curl http://localhost:9998/ → JSON containing name open_taki, version, features.
5. Furthermore, to show that it functions as a Tika replacement, also test the actual Tika endpoint: PUT a text file to /rmeta/text (or is it /tika/text?) with Content-Type — check the handler. The guide says "same API (PUT /rmeta/text)". Let's check the signature of handleRmetaText and how it expects the request. I'll do a quick grep.

Actually, let me check which request format /rmeta/text expects, so I can do a functional verification with a sample text file (this works without an LLM). Let me take a look at that handler.

action.command: cd /workspace && grep -n "handleRmetaText\|handleTikaText" main.go | head -5 && sed -n "$(grep -n 'func (s \*Server) handleRmetaText' main.go | cut -d: -f1),+60p" main.go

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cd /workspace && grep -n \"handleRmetaText\\|handleTikaText\" main.go | head -5 && sed -n \"$(grep -n 'func (s \\*Server) handleRmetaText' main.go | cut -d: -f1),+60p\" main.go", "security_risk": "LOW", "summary": "Inspect handleRmetaText handler"}
